description: The Network Outage Reporting System is the Federal Communications Commission's database of reports of significant outages on communications networks in the United States. Set up after the attacks of 11 September 2001, it requires wireline, wireless, cable, satellite, interconnected VoIP and signalling providers to file notifications, initial reports and final reports on outages that meet thresholds of duration and users affected, including any cellular outage of 30 minutes or more that meets the thresholds and outages that affect 911 call centres, with the cause, duration, users affected and restoration. The FCC's Cybersecurity and Communications Reliability Division analyses NORS to spot trends and promote best practices. Filings are confidential, but since 30 September 2022 the FCC gives direct read-only access to NORS and DIRS filings to agencies of the states, the District of Columbia, Tribal nations, territories and the federal government. Coverage: the United States, from 2004 onward. Format and access: web filing system; access only for providers and authorised government agencies, free of charge to them and not licensed for public reuse; outage summaries and reports are published occasionally. Caveats: raw reports are not public; thresholds exclude small outages; cause categories are self-reported. Simulation uses: outage frequency, duration and cause statistics for reliability and restoration modelling, and 911 dependency analysis. Related records: FCC DIRS status reports cover disasters, and the FCC Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative sets roaming and mutual aid duties.
